1364	### 11.5 Adapters
1365	
1366	`@piton/belay` exports `ClaudeCodeAdapter`, `CodexAdapter` and
1367	`OpenCodeAdapter`. Each extends the abstract `belay-agent-adapter`
1368	(`description`, `targetId`, `instructionFile`, `referenceRoot`).
1369	
1370	| | Claude Code (`claude-code`) | Codex (`codex`) | OpenCode (`opencode`) |
1371	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1372	| Instruction file | `CLAUDE.md` | `AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` |
1373	| Reference root | `.claude/reference` | `.codex/reference` | `.opencode/reference` |
1374	| Skill | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, YAML frontmatter `name`, `description` | `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, same frontmatter | `.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Name 1–64 lowercase alphanumerics with single hyphens, matching its directory; description 1–1024 characters. |
1375	| Command | Translated: `.claude/skills/x-<name>/SKILL.md` with `disable-model-invocation: true`, invoked as `/x-<name>` | Translated: `.agents/skills/x-<name>/SKILL.md` plus `agents/openai.yaml` with `policy: allow_implicit_invocation: false`, invoked as `$x-<name>` | Native: `.opencode/commands/x-<name>.md`, identity from the filename, invoked as `/x-<name>` |
1376	| Agent | `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, frontmatter `name`, `description`, optional `tools`, `model` | `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` with `name`, `description`, `developer_instructions` (role, prompt, extras), optional `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode` | `.opencode/agents/<name>.md`, frontmatter `description`, `mode` (`primary`, `subagent` or `all`; always explicit, default `subagent`), optional `model`, `permission`; identity from the filename |
1377	| Native options | agent: `tools`, `model`. skill and command: `allowed-tools`, `model`. | agent: `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`. None for skills or commands. | agent: `mode`, `model`, `permission`. command: `agent`, `model`. None for skills. |
1378	| Loading | Ancestor guidance loads at startup; nested guidance loads when Claude reads in that subtree. | A root-to-working-directory chain is built at run start. A same-directory `AGENTS.override.md` shadows generated guidance (`shadowed-instruction`); an instruction byte limit applies (`instruction-over-budget`). | Searches upward from the working directory and prefers `AGENTS.md` over its `CLAUDE.md` fallback. Nested files are not assumed to load (`unguaranteed-instruction-scope` unless configured). It also discovers Claude and `.agents` skills. |
1379	
1380	Rules for every adapter:
1381	
1382	- **Pipeline:** take the emitted, validated constructs from Piton, build one
1383	  output plan per adapter, resolve instruction placement and reference
1384	  destinations, check shared paths and cross-discovery across the whole plan,
1385	  serialize, validate links, metadata, names and output ownership, then write.
1386	- Every adapter carries `documentationChecked` (currently `2026-09-21`): the
1387	  date its target's documentation was last checked, recorded in the
1388	  manifest's `targets`.
1389	- Constructs are consumed **after** imports and inheritance resolve. Each of
1390	  the four constructs is mapped explicitly for each target.
1391	- An adapter distinguishes native support, translation and unsupported
1392	  behaviour, and fails with an actionable diagnostic when required behaviour
1393	  can't be represented.
1394	- Model and permission settings are applied **only when configured
1395	  explicitly**. Absent settings are omitted so native defaults apply. Native
1396	  options are validated against the target platform version, and role,
1397	  prompt and other prose never get copied into metadata fields.
1398	- **A prompt that requests restraint is not an enforced restriction.** An
1399	  adapter claims enforcement only for controls the platform applies, and never
1400	  translates permissions in a way that silently widens access. Claude's
1401	  `allowed-tools` and subagent `tools` serve different purposes; neither is a
1402	  portable sandbox. Requesting an enforced restriction the adapter can't
1403	  represent is a diagnostic.
1404	- An adapter never silently turns an agent into a skill, or a command into an
1405	  automatically invoked skill, when that changes how it activates.
1406	- Names are normalized before planning, and commands keep the `x-` prefix
1407	  after normalization. Collisions are errors (`name-collision`,
1408	  `output-collision`) unless the artifacts are identical in content,
1409	  reference resolution and activation.
1410	- **Multiple adapters:** the tools read each other's files (Codex and
1411	  OpenCode both read `AGENTS.md`; OpenCode also discovers `.claude/skills` and
1412	  `.agents/skills`), so with several adapters Belay plans one shared project
1413	  and writes each artifact once, where the tools find it:
1414	  - the **first adapter listed owns the one reference tree**, and every
1415	    adapter links into it;
1416	  - an instruction file several adapters place at one path (`AGENTS.md`) is
1417	    **written once**, by the first of them listed;
1418	  - OpenCode **writes no copy of a skill** Claude Code or Codex already
1419	    writes where it discovers it, and links to theirs;
1420	  - a command's `x-` skill that OpenCode would discover is an error
1421	    (`cross-discovery-activation`) unless `opencode.json` hides it with a
1422	    skill permission (`"permission": {"skill": {"x-*": "deny"}}`; the last
1423	    matching pattern decides) or `crossDiscovery` is set;
1424	  - a skill OpenCode finds in two directories (all three adapters enabled)
1425	    is a `cross-target-discovery` warning, since nothing in the project can
1426	    stop it.
1427	
1428	  `crossDiscovery: separate` means each tool's tree is deployed apart: every
1429	  adapter writes its own complete tree, and incompatible writes to one path
1430	  are rejected (`output-collision`). The whole plan is still checked before
1431	  anything is written.
1432	- Generated links (from `@{...}` references) are relative to the file that
1433	  contains them and must point at planned outputs (`broken-reference-link`).
1434	  Markdown links you write in prose are text and are never checked.
1435	- Discovery metadata and body are emitted exactly once. Frontmatter is written
1436	  with a format-aware YAML or TOML encoder. Generated filenames and native
1437	  metadata are checked against the target's schema, and unsupported requested
1438	  capabilities are diagnosed before anything is written.
1439	
1440	Adapter specifics:
1441	
1442	- **Claude Code.** A skill's directory name is its frontmatter `name`. Claude
1443	  Code still reads `.claude/commands/`, but Belay emits commands only as
1444	  skills, never both for one command. Agent identity comes from the
1445	  normalized name, never a rendered heading. `allowed-tools`/`tools` are
1446	  never copied to another platform without a mapping.
1447	- **Codex.** Belay never writes `AGENTS.override.md` to win precedence.
1448	  Guidance below the directory a session starts in is not guaranteed to load.
1449	  The byte limit checked is `instructionByteLimit` (11.1). Commands never use
1450	  deprecated custom prompts or an invented `.codex/commands/`.
1451	  `developer_instructions` is one valid TOML string; a generic `tools` list is
1452	  never mapped to an invented field. Only the standalone custom-agent format is
1453	  targeted. Codex's sandbox and approval settings govern execution and
1454	  guidance can't override them; tool or model settings on a command are
1455	  diagnosed. A command must produce both its files, and an agent's TOML must
1456	  parse with `name`, `description` and `developer_instructions`.
1457	- **OpenCode.** Don't assume Claude's nested loading or Codex's chain. Extra
1458	  guidance files go through its explicit `instructions` configuration when a
1459	  deployment needs them, never by loading every nested instruction globally;
1460	  if shape scoping is required and can't be guaranteed, that is an error.
1461	  Unrecognized frontmatter never enforces policy. `model` values are
1462	  provider-qualified. Argument placeholders written in a command prompt are
1463	  kept. `allowed-tools` is never an enforced command setting. Agents use
1464	  `permission`, not the deprecated `tools`, mapped only when the meaning is
1465	  equivalent: allow/ask/deny is not a tool list, and ambiguous conversions are
1466	  rejected.
1467	
1468	Other Belay diagnostics include `invalid-artifact-name`,
1469	`missing-command-prefix`, `description-too-long`, `output-outside-project`,
1470	`unowned-output`, `duplicated-content` and `unrepresentable-reference`.
1471	
1472	### 11.6 Guarantees
1473	
1474	- Identical source, configuration, directory state and toolchain produce
1475	  identical bytes. Instructions combined into one file have a stable order.
1476	- Frontmatter values are quoted and escaped for the target format.
1477	- A missing reference target is reported instead of emitting a broken link.
1478	- Unsupported metadata is reported instead of being claimed as enforced.
1479	- Generated files are tracked in `.piton/manifest.json`, so cleanup never
1480	  deletes files users wrote. Its `targets` records, for each target, the
1481	  documentation date the generated files were validated against.
1482	- Failures name the source anchor and property. Output stays inside its
1483	  configured boundaries.
1484	
1485	### 11.7 Open decisions
1486	
1487	`spec/scope/belay/Decisions.pi` lists what is not decided. Tooling should say
1488	it is unspecified rather than guess:
1489	
1490	- Placement of instructions outside `shapeRoot`.
1491	- The types of `tools`, `allowed-tools` and `model`, and their mapping per
1492	  adapter.
1493	- Naming: skill filename normalization, command name normalization before the
1494	  `x-` prefix, acronym splitting and collision handling.
1495	- Whether workflows stay compositions of the four constructs. Do not add a
1496	  `workflow` keyword just because examples describe agent processes.
1497	- How platform-specific adapter options are written.
1498	
1499	Do not present any of these as settled. If your work depends on one, raise it
1500	with the user.
1501	
1502	## 12. Package management
1503	
1504	Packages are git repositories, managed as **vendored dependencies**. Installed
1505	packages are stored inside the project and committed to version control, and
1506	the tooling adds, updates, removes and inspects them. Nothing is fetched at
1507	compile time.
1508	
1509	- **Offering packages.** A repository declares packages with `piton-package`
1510	  anchors (`PitonPackage` from `@piton/packaging`: `name`, `root`,
1511	  `dependencies`). A package anchor can live anywhere in the specbase but must
1512	  be listed under `packages:` in `piton.config.pi`. A package's `root` is
1513	  relative to `piton.config.pi`, like the project's own root. **`packages:` is what the
1514	  repository offers to other projects; a project never installs its own
1515	  packages.** One repository can offer several packages, each with its own
1516	  root and dependencies.
1517	- **Names.** `name` is what the package installs under. It exists because it
1518	  can be kebab-case (`my-package`), which an anchor name can't. Left out, the
1519	  anchor's own name is used. **Package names are flat: no `/`.** Names like
1520	  `@piton/belay` are only for the packages bundled with the compiler.
1521	- **Dependencies.** `dependencies:` lists git URLs, each with an optional
1522	  `commit:`, `tag:` or `branch:` on an indented line beneath it (a dictionary
1523	  item right after the URL). **Only one pin per URL**; more is
1524	  `multiple-pins`. Without a pin, the latest commit on the default branch is
1525	  used. **Pins are strings**: `@piton/config` types them as strings, so
1526	  `tag: 1.0` stays `"1.0"`. Other pin diagnostics are `dangling-pin` and
1527	  `unknown-pin`.
1528	- **Picking packages.** A repository can offer several packages. You get all
1529	  of them unless you list the ones you want with `packages:` under the URL:
1530	  `packages: [ui-kit]`.
1531	- **Project and package dependencies are separate.** The project's apply only
1532	  to the project, and each package declares its own.
1533	- **No nested dependencies.** When two packages need the same package at
1534	  different versions, **the one with the newest commit wins** and a warning is
1535	  shown.
1536	- **Installation.** Each package goes into `tethers/<name>`, next to
1537	  `piton.config.pi`, with the files from its `root`. A repository offering
1538	  `ui-kit` and `my-package` gives `tethers/ui-kit` and `tethers/my-package`.
1539	  Tethering removes every trace of git. A repository that offers no packages
1540	  is installed whole, under the name its URL implies.
1541	- **Importing.** An installed package is a location placeholder:
1542	  `from my-package import X`, `use my-package`, `use my-package/MyAnchor`.
1543	  Normal path resolution applies below it. A missing package is a compiler
1544	  error.
1545	- **Lock file.** `.piton/tether.lock`, next to `piton.config.pi`, keeps each
1546	  tethered package's URL, commit and a hash of its files. `tether` and
1547	  `update` write it, and it is committed with the project.
1548	- **Conflicts.** Before tether, update or any other operation on an installed
1549	  package, the tooling compares its files with the lock file and goes ahead
1550	  only if nothing changed. If the files were edited, it says so and asks the
1551	  user to untether (or `piton update --force` to discard the edits).
1552	
1553	The commands:
1554	
1555	- `piton tether` on its own installs everything in `dependencies`. Given a
1556	  source URL, it adds it to `dependencies` in `piton.config.pi` and installs
1557	  it. `--as <name>` installs under another name.
1558	- `piton update [packages...] [--force] [--diff]` reinstalls from
1559	  `dependencies`, all packages when none are named. `--force` replaces a
1560	  package even if it was edited, discarding the edits with a warning;
1561	  `--diff` prints a coloured unified diff of every file each update changed.
1562	- `piton untether <package>` moves the package from `tethers/` to
1563	  `<root>/untethered/` and rewrites the imports that named it, making it the
1564	  project's own source. `--as <name>` renames it; `--no-rewrite` only moves
1565	  it.
1566	- `piton remove <package>` deletes an installed package and removes it from
1567	  `dependencies`. It refuses if the files were edited or if anything still
1568	  imports the package.
1569	
1570	## 13. CLI reference
1571	
1572	Every command prints what it produced first, then a one-line outcome (✓ or
1573	✗), and its problems last: diagnostics, errors and warnings with their help
1574	and notes, then the error and warning count. On a terminal the output is
1575	coloured and paths are marked `+`/`-`; piped or with `NO_COLOR`, it is plain
1576	text and stdout carries the bare results.
1577	
1578	| Command | Behaviour |
1579	| --- | --- |
1580	| `piton check [paths...]` | Validates syntax, imports, references, types, inheritance, composition, exports and circular dependencies, reporting errors and warnings. Writes nothing. Exits 0 when there are no errors and 1 otherwise. Paths are optional files, directories or globs; the default is the project (or every `.pi` file under the working directory when there's no `piton.config.pi`). |
1581	| `piton build [config] [--dry-run]` | Builds the project configured by `piton.config.pi` (or the given config). Writes renderer output to `<output>/<path under root>.<ext>` (defaults: `./dist`, JSON), so `spec/components/Button.pi` becomes `dist/components/Button.json`: the entry file plus every file holding something the entry's exports reference. A registered framework's output replaces it unless the config sets `output` or `renderer`, which asks for both. Records every file in `.piton/manifest.json`. The whole plan is validated before anything is written. `--dry-run` reports without writing. |
1582	| `piton compile <path> [--renderer json\|yaml\|markdown] [--write] [--dependencies]` | Compiles one file to stdout (JSON by default): one key per export. `--write` writes `<file>.<ext>` next to each input and is required for globs. `--dependencies` wraps the result as `{"value": "<compiled output as a string>", "dependencies": [absolute source paths]}` so build tools know what to watch; bundled package files are left out. |
1583	| `piton format [path] [--check]` | Applies canonical formatting (4-space indents, constraint spacing, sorted and wrapped imports, no `.pi` in import paths, a space after `//`). `--check` reports without writing. `piton format -` reads source from stdin and writes the formatted text to stdout. It **only splits overflowing lines and never rejoins a paragraph**, so rewrap edited prose by hand, and don't reflow `key: value` blocks as prose. |
1584	| `piton reach [targets...] [--no-unreachable] [--no-paths]` | Starting from files, globs or anchor names (the entry by default), follows outgoing imports, references, inheritance and composition, direct and transitive. Reports what is reachable with its depth and the path taken, and what is unreachable. The flags hide the last two. Use it to find dead spec. Grouped by source, with a summary. No diagnostics; always exits 0. |
1585	| `piton slice <target> [--adapter <target>]` | Prints the part of the spec one thing depends on, as one Markdown document for an agent's prompt. The target is `file.pi#Anchor`, `file.pi#Anchor.property`, `file.pi#variable`, or a bare name looked up across the project (an error when more than one file declares it). Follows, transitively: what an anchor extends, every base that also declares a property, anchors named by type constraints, what a value read (`${Other.x}`, variables), and what it references or embeds. Imports alone bring nothing in. A whole anchor needs all its properties and bases; slicing a property leaves out the anchor's other properties; a reference to a property needs only that property. It also includes the **chain** from the project's entry down to the target (`Specification.Tooling`, `Tooling.cli`, `Cli.commands`): the shortest path the build takes, each link only that one property and not followed further. An export of the entry, a variable, and a file the build doesn't reach have no chain. Order: the target, then its dependencies nearest first (source order breaks ties), then the chain outermost first, so the same source prints the same bytes. Each declaration appears once, headed by its name as written (`SaveButton.color`), with its file, what it extends, its type and what it reads. References and embeds are written as names; cycles are followed until they come back around. Every path it prints is relative to the directory it runs in, and it finds the project by looking upward for `piton.config.pi`. `--adapter claude-code` (any Belay target the project builds) cites the compiled output instead: each location and every reference links to where `piton build` writes it (an embedded anchor to the section that embeds it), and no `.pi` file is ever cited; an abstract base or an anchor that is only read has no document of its own and is described without one. With `--adapter` the target itself must be something the build writes out. Markdown links the author wrote pass through unchanged. Exits 1 on errors. |
1586	| `piton init [directory] [--template <group/name>] [--adapter <id>...] [--list]` | Starts a new project from a template compiled into the compiler (no network needed). Templates come in groups: `piton/minimal` (plain Piton to JSON), `piton/library` (a package others can tether), `belay/application` (a shape instruction placed in `src/`, a skill, an agent and a command) and `belay/minimal` (the Belay config and one skill). Without a directory it first asks for the project's name and creates that directory (an empty answer, or no terminal, uses the working one). Then it asks for a group and a template (`--template belay` asks only for the template), and for a Belay template, which adapters to build for: a checklist of Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode with the template's default (Claude Code) checked, or `--adapter`, repeated or comma-separated. The chosen adapters replace the config's import and `adapters` list, and a template's `.adapters/<id>/` files (like OpenCode's `opencode.json`) are written only for the adapters chosen. Templates are the `group/name` directories in the compiler repo's `create-templates/`, each with a one-line `.template` description that is not written out; adding one is adding a directory, and every template must check cleanly, be formatted, and build. `--list` describes the groups and templates and does nothing else. With no terminal, a full template name is required. It never overwrites a file: if any it would write exists, it names each and writes none, and cancelling a question writes nothing. Prints each written path on stdout, then a summary and the next commands on stderr. Exits 1 on errors. |
1587	| `piton loc [paths...]` | Counts total, code, comment and blank lines per file, with a summary. Defaults to the project. No diagnostics; always exits 0. |
1588	| `piton lsp` | Runs the language server over stdio (section 14). |
1589	| `piton agent [claude] [--print-fluency] [args...]` | Launches the agent with a short project primer plus this fluency prompt (the project's `FLUENCY_PROMPT.md`, or the copy built into the compiler), passed to `claude` as `--append-system-prompt`. Extra arguments go to the agent. `--print-fluency` prints the prompt and does nothing else. |
1590	| `piton tether [source] [--as name]` | See section 12. |
1591	| `piton update [packages...] [--force] [--diff]` | See section 12. |
1592	| `piton untether <package> [--as name] [--no-rewrite]` | See section 12. |
1593	| `piton remove <package>` | See section 12. |
1594	
1595	Each CLI command in the spec is a `cli-command` anchor
1596	(`spec/scope/tooling/cli/index.pi`) with `commandName`, `positionalArguments`
1597	and `namedArguments`.
1598	
1599	## 14. Language server, editors, and JavaScript
1600	
1601	`piton lsp` provides, from the spec's feature list:
1602	
1603	- Diagnostics (not for missing optional properties), completion, hover (type,
1604	  source, documentation, inheritance chain, export status and compiled
1605	  interpretation), go-to-definition, find-references, and rename across the
1606	  whole specbase.
1607	- Auto-import, import organization, and code actions: import a missing
1608	  symbol, create an unresolved anchor, add an export, qualify an ambiguous
1609	  reference, resolve a simple inheritance conflict.
1610	- Document and workspace symbols, semantic highlighting, inlay hints
1611	  (resolved types, inherited origins, composition sources), formatting,
1612	  folding and selection ranges.
1613	- Inheritance, composition (`+`, `++`), override and conflict resolution;
1614	  reference resolution; validation and type information for expressions in
1615	  `{}`, `${}`, `#{}` and `@{}`; export validation; module resolution; cycle
1616	  detection (circular imports are fine and not reported).
1617	- Related-symbol navigation, a hierarchy view, resolved-value and provenance
1618	  inspection, compiled-output preview, source-to-output mapping, unused and
1619	  redundant definition detection, and documentation integration.
1620	- Incremental analysis and workspace indexing.
1621	- Diagnostics cover Belay semantics as well as Piton. Import organization
1622	  flags unused, duplicate, invalid and overly broad imports. Cycle detection
1623	  also catches an anchor that ends up extending itself, and shows the cycle.
1624	
1625	There is no signature help.
1626	
1627	Completion rules: never suggest things that don't exist; offer nothing on an
1628	empty value (`property: `), because prose probably follows; offer nothing
1629	after a `.` inside a string.
1630	
1631	Editing rules every editor must follow, through the LSP or the editor
1632	extension:
1633	
1634	- Enter after a colon that opens a dictionary or anchor property starts a new
1635	  line indented one level deeper.
1636	- Enter on a blank line inside a dictionary or anchor starts a new line one
1637	  level shallower.
1638	- Format-on-save is optional. It adds the space after `//` and touches nothing
1639	  else that is commented.
1640	
1641	Supported editors and their highlighters (spec): VS Code (TextMate plus LSP);
1642	Emacs, Helix and Zed (tree-sitter plus LSP); Neovim and Vim (vim syntax);
1643	JetBrains (`jetbrains`); Sublime (sublime-syntax); Kate (KSyntaxHighlighting).
1644	Every editor gets full LSP support. The integrations live under `editors/`.
1645	
1646	**Consuming Piton from JavaScript.** `packages/vite-plugin-piton` imports
1647	`.pi` files as modules, with HMR, dependency tracking (through
1648	`piton compile --dependencies`) and virtual modules. Each export in the Piton
1649	file is a named export, and the default export is the whole file, the same as
1650	`piton compile` gives:
1651	
1652	```ts
1653	import { SaveButton } from '../spec/app.pi';
1654	import spec from '../spec/app.pi';
1655	
1656	const button = SaveButton;
1657	const cancel = spec.CancelButton;
1658	```
1659	
1660	It has a configurable default renderer (`renderer: 'json' | 'yaml' |
1661	'markdown'`), and the renderers can also be imported as functions
1662	(`vite-plugin-piton/renderers`) and used inline. `packages/astro-piton` is an
1663	Astro integration that wraps the Vite plugin.
1664	
1665	## 15. Working on a specbase
1666	
1667	1. **Orient.** Open `piton.config.pi` to find `root`, `entry`, `output`, the
1668	   frameworks, the adapters, `codeRoot` and `shapeRoot`. Read the entry file,
1669	   usually `spec/index.pi`, because its exports are the compilation roots.
1670	   Follow the `index.pi` files down through the modules. In this repository,
1671	   `spec/index.pi` exports `Specification` (FoundingThesis, Language, Tooling,
1672	   Belay, PackageManagement) plus the skills and command in `spec/agent/`.
1673	2. **Read compiled reference for overview, and source for truth.**
1674	   `<referenceRoot>/**/*.md` is easy to browse, and its links are lazy, so
1675	   follow them only when relevant.
1676	3. **Edit the `.pi` source**, following the conventions around it:
1677	   - one exported anchor per file, named after the file;
1678	   - `index.pi` files that re-export with `from ./X export *`;
1679	   - abstract anchors exported with a keyword, and shared abstracts in a
1680	     `lib/` folder;
1681	   - lowerCamelCase property names;
1682	   - SCREAMING_CASE for exported constant lists;
1683	   - prose in string blocks, and structure in keys and lists;
1684	   - `@{X}` to link related documents;
1685	   - examples inside fences wrapped in a `\\\` escape block.
1686	4. **Keep imports honest.** Use `use` for keywords and `from ... import` for
1687	   names; a file often needs both. A new file only compiles if the entry
1688	   reaches it, so export it through an index or reference it.
1689	5. **Validate.**
1690	   - Run `piton check`.
1691	   - `piton check` does **not** compile the examples inside escape blocks
1692	     (they are literal text). When you edit spec examples, extract each ` ```piton ` block,
1693	     run `piton compile` on it, and compare with any ` ```json ` block that
1694	     follows. Remember that compile output has only exported names.
1695	   - Run `piton build`, then look at the diff of the generated files.
1696	   - Run `piton reach` to confirm new anchors are reached.
1697	   - Run `piton format --check`.
1698	6. **Never hand-edit generated files.** That includes `CLAUDE.md` and
1699	   `AGENTS.md` under `codeRoot`, everything under `.claude/`, `.codex/`,
1700	   `.agents/`, `.opencode/` and the build output directory that is listed in
1701	   `.piton/manifest.json`, and the files in `.piton/` themselves.
1702	7. **Keep implementation and spec in agreement.** The implementation is judged
1703	   against the spec. When they disagree, report it instead of quietly bending
1704	   the spec to fit. Trust `piton compile` for how things behave today, and
1705	   flag the gap.
1706	
1707	## 16. Where the compiler differs from the spec
1708	
1709	Checked with `piton compile` and `piton build`:
1710	
1711	- The CLI has a few things the spec doesn't name: `build --dry-run`,
1712	  `tether --as`, agent argument passthrough, the `reach` flags, and
1713	  `format` with no path or `-`.
1714	
1715	- **Paragraph breaks.** The spec says a blank line in a string block starts a
1716	  new paragraph. The compiler joins the paragraphs with a single `\n`, which
1717	  Markdown output renders as one paragraph with a soft line break.
1718	
1719	Known limitations, where the spec is silent and the compiler's choice may
1720	surprise you:
1721	
1722	- A `/`-rooted import inside an installed package resolves against the
1723	  consuming project's root, not the package's. Use relative imports inside a
1724	  package.
1725	- A required property from an abstract is not satisfied by a value inherited
1726	  from a concrete base (`needs Thing extends Base`, where `Base` supplies it):
1727	  the keyword's anchor comes last, and its value-less declaration wins. Give
1728	  the value on the anchor itself.
1729	- `piton check` with no paths checks what the entry reaches, so a file that
1730	  nothing imports is not checked. Name it: `piton check path/to/file.pi`.
1731	- **Prose directly in an anchor body is silently dropped.** `anchor A:` with
1732	  only a line of text under it (no key) compiles to an empty anchor, with no
1733	  diagnostic. Always put prose under a key, such as `description:`.
1734	- Mixed-type equality is simply unequal: `{1 == "1"}` is `false`, not an
1735	  error. The spec says `==` works on every type but doesn't spell this out.
1736	- Which constructs each adapter requires a `description` for (section 11.2)
1737	  is hardcoded in `crates/piton-belay/src/adapter.rs`, not declared in the
1738	  adapter `.pi` files.
1739

Exit code 1
# File Tree Scope

## How To Build

A FileTreeScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A FileTreeScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Title

null

## Counted

false

## Height

fill

## Scrolls

true

## Panel

It has no header: its contents start at its top edge, on the theme's base surface.
It shows no count of what it lists.
It fills the height its sidebar's other panels leave.
Its contents scroll on their own when they are taller than it, with a permanent scrollbar along its right, as the ScrollbarScope says.

## Concept

### Pitch

A tree view of the files and folders in the current [ProjectDirectoryScope](../../../scope/project-directory/index.md#project-directory-scope), for finding a file and opening it.

### Shape

#### Description

Folders are listed before files, both by name, and a folder's contents are shown when it is expanded. It scrolls with a [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope). Until a project is picked it reads "No project open", as the [NoProjectStateScope](../../../scope/no-project/index.md#no-project-state-scope) says.

#### Look

The tree sits on the darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, a step darker than the ribbon's command area, and in light mode a step lighter than it instead. Each row is 24 pixels tall: an icon, then the name 8 pixels after it, in regular text, with no chevrons. Rows start 16 pixels from the tree's left edge, and each level of a folder's contents is indented 24 pixels further, so a file's icon sits beneath its folder's name. Clicking a folder's row expands or collapses it.
A folder shows an outlined folder icon, the same whether it is expanded or not. A file shows an outlined file icon; a .pi file's is a code file icon, and the project's piton.config.pi a settings file icon in the theme's orange. Icons are in muted text colour, except that the spec location's folder, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../../../scope/project-locations/index.md#project-locations-scope) says, and its .pi files take Spec's colour, and the code location's folder takes Code's colour, of the [PromptModesScope](../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope), each on its icon alone. A folder or file whose name starts with a dot, other than a .gitignore or similar file, and anything git ignores, is dimmed, name and icon both, as tertiary text is.
The selected row, the file open in the editor or the folder last clicked, has a background of the ribbon's command area colour, #222222 in dark mode, inset 8 pixels from either side of the tree, with softly rounded corners, and its name in semibold. Hovering a row gives it the same background, fainter. There are no lines between rows.

#### Refreshing

The tree refreshes by itself when files or folders are added, removed, or renamed on disk, keeping expanded folders open and the selection in place.

#### Git Status

Each name is coloured by its status in the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope), in that status's color; unchanged names keep the default color, and a folder shows the status it takes from its contents, so a change stays visible while its folder is collapsed.

#### Diff Button

A new, untracked, or modified file has a small diff button, an icon with a "Show the changes" tooltip, at the right end of its row. Clicking it opens the file's [DiffViewScope](../diff-view/index.md#diff-view-scope) rather than the file itself.

#### Opening

Clicking a file opens it, as the [OpenFileScope](../../../scope/open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says.

#### Context Menu

Right-clicking a file or folder, or the empty space beneath the rows, opens a menu there, with, in order:

- "New File…", with a file-plus icon, and "New Folder…", with a folder-plus icon: in a folder right-clicked, in the folder holding a file right-clicked, or at the top of the project for the empty space
- a separator, then "Rename…", with a pencil icon, and "Delete", with a trash icon, for a file or folder only, not the empty space

# Git Panel Scope

## How To Build

A GitPanelScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A GitPanelScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Title

null

## Counted

false

## Height

fit

## Scrolls

false

## Panel

It has no header: its contents start at its top edge, on the theme's base surface.
It shows no count of what it lists.
It is only as tall as its contents need, taking no more of its sidebar's height.
Its contents never scroll: it is as tall as they are.

## Concept

### Pitch

A very basic git panel for the repository the ProjectDirectoryScope is in, as the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope) knows it: see what has changed at a glance, write a commit message, commit, push, and pull.

### Shape

#### Description

A compact panel. It is shown only while the project is inside a git repository.

#### Look

The panel's top row, the branch, is its header: 32 pixels tall, on the ribbon's tab row colour, #333333 in dark mode. Beneath it, the panel's body is on the ribbon's command area colour, #222222 in dark mode, with 8 pixels of padding at either side and at the bottom, and 4 pixels between one thing and the next. There is no line between the header and the body, nor between the file tree and the header: the change of colour is the edge. Every box and button in it is square, with no rounded corners and no border.

#### Branch

The top row shows a branch icon, then the branch from the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope), or "Detached HEAD", in regular text, beside how many commits it is ahead of its upstream (↑) and behind it (↓), muted, each only when not zero. At the right end are a Pull button, a cloud-download icon, and a Push button, a cloud-upload icon, ghost icon buttons with tooltips.

#### Summary

Below the branch, a line counts the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope)'s changes, leaving out any kind with none, as "2 modified · 1 untracked", or "No changes". At the right end of that line, how many lines were added (+, in green) and removed (−, in red). The count is in small, muted text. The files themselves are not listed, since the [FileTreeScope](../file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope) shows them. The summary refreshes as the [GitScope](../../../scope/git/index.md#git-scope) does, and straight after anything the panel does.

#### Commit Notes

Above the message box, a box for each commit note, in the order they were added, on the ribbon's tab row colour, holding the note in small text that wraps onto as many lines as it needs, and can be edited. A small button to remove it shows at its top right while it is hovered. Each task that adds a note, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) says, adds a one-line summary of what it changed, once the harness has written it, quickly, in the same way as a written

##### Message

from what the task asked and the harness's own summary of what

it did, at most 72 characters in the imperative mood, as commit-note.pi, of the [BakedSystemPromptsScope](../../../scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts-scope), asks. Notes are saved with the project's data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../../scope/project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, as they are added, edited, and removed, so they survive a restart, and are never themselves committed.

#### Message

A commit message box, a [GrowingTextInputScope](../growing-text-input/index.md#growing-text-input-scope) growing to 10 rows at most, so it starts at a single row. On the tree's darkest surface, #111111 in dark mode, in the editor's monospace font, it reads "Commit Message…" while empty.

#### Writing AMessage

A "Generate" button, with a sparkles icon, on the ribbon's tab row colour, at the left of the row beneath the message box, has the harness write the commit message from what has changed, and puts it in the message box, replacing what was there. It is quick: a small, fast model, at low effort, with no tools, handed only the list of changed files and as much of the diff as fits in a small, fixed amount. The message is a summary line of at most 72 characters in the imperative mood, followed, only if it helps, by a few short bullet points, as commit-message.pi, of the [BakedSystemPromptsScope](../../../scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts-scope), asks. The button is disabled while there are no changes.

#### Committing

A primary "Commit" button, at the right end of that row, on the ribbon's button colour, #444444 in dark mode, commits every change, new files included. The commit message is what was typed, then a blank line, then each note that isn't blank as a line of its own starting "- "; with nothing typed, it is the notes alone. Once committed, the message box and the notes are cleared. It is disabled while there is neither a message nor a note, or there are no changes.

#### Pushing And Pulling

Push pushes the branch, setting its upstream on origin first if it has none.
Pull fetches the branch's upstream. With nothing new it says the branch is already up to date. When only the upstream has moved on, the branch fast-forwards to it. When both have moved on, the upstream is merged in automatically, as long as the merge has no conflicts. If it would conflict, the pull is cancelled before anything changes: the branch, its files, and the index stay exactly as they were, no merge is left in progress, and an error names the files that would have conflicted. Pull is disabled while the branch has no upstream.

#### Feedback

While the panel is committing, pushing, pulling, or writing a message, that button shows a spinner and the others are disabled. Committing, pushing, and pulling say so in a notification when they succeed; a pull says whether it was already up to date, pulled, or pulled and merged. Anything that fails says why in an error notification.

# Sidebar Scope

## How To Build

A SidebarScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A SidebarScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

A column along the left or right of the main window, holding panels one above the other, each a tool for the work beside it.

### Shape

#### Description

Every sidebar is a sidebar, as its own scope says: it names the side it runs along, how wide it starts and how narrow it can be dragged, and the panels it holds, and those decide how it is drawn. It runs along its side, with a thin line down the edge where it meets what it sits beside, and is resized by dragging that edge. It holds its panels one above the other, across its full width, with a single thin line between one panel and the next.

#### Sidebars

- left: the [ProjectSidebarScope](../project-sidebar/index.md#project-sidebar-scope), along the left of the body, for finding your way around the project
- right: the [ReferencedSpecSidebarScope](../referenced-spec-sidebar/index.md#referenced-spec-sidebar-scope), at the right of the message list while a task runs

#### Panels

A panel is one tool in a sidebar, as its own scope says. What it is like follows from four things it names:

- its title: a panel with a title has a header reading it; one without has no header
- whether it is counted: a counted panel's header shows how many rows it lists, muted, at its right
- its height: a panel fills the height its sidebar's other panels leave, fits its contents, or shares the height left with the other panels that share it, by a line dragged between them
- whether it scrolls: one that scrolls has a [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope) of its own when its contents are taller than it

#### Headers

A panel's header is slightly contrasting to the panel's body: the header is on the theme's raised surface, a small step toward the viewer, and the body on its base surface, as the sidebar is, so the header reads as part of the panel, marked off from its body, with no line between them.
---------
# Project Sidebar Scope

## How To Build

A ProjectSidebarScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A ProjectSidebarScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Side

left

## Width

260

## Min Width

160

## Panels

- [FileTreeScope](../file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope)
- [GitPanelScope](../git-panel/index.md#git-panel-scope)

## Sidebar

It runs along the left of what it sits beside, with a thin line down its right edge, where the two meet. It is resized by dragging that edge: it starts 260 pixels wide and can't be dragged narrower than 160.
It holds its panels one above the other, in the order it lists them, each across its full width. A single thin line, in the theme's line colour, lies between one panel and the next, never two, unless the next panel says its own change of colour is the edge. A panel that isn't shown for the moment takes no room and leaves no line.
It is on the theme's base surface, as its panels' bodies are.

## Concept

### Pitch

The [SidebarScope](../sidebar/index.md#sidebar-scope) along the left of the main window's body, holding the tools for finding your way around the project.

### Shape

#### Description

Runs the full height of the body, beneath the ribbon, to the left of everything else in it. The file tree fills it from the top, and the git panel sits along the bottom, underneath it, taking only the height it needs.

#### Others

It is the body's only sidebar on the left. While a task runs, a second one, the running task's referenced spec, slides out at the right of the message list, as the [MessageList](../../../scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list) says.

# Project Locations Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

Where in a project its spec and its code are, and which files are counted as being there.

### Shape

#### Description

A project's locations are set in the piton.config.pi of the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../project-directory/index.md#project-directory-scope), each a path relative to the project directory.

#### Locations

- the spec location is `root`, of its piton-config anchor
- the code location is `codeRoot`, of its belay-config framework
- the shape location, which mirrors the code location folder for folder, is `shapeRoot`, of its belay-config framework

#### Missing

A location missing from the config is left out of whatever would use it, or, where it can't be left out, what needs it says it couldn't be read.

#### Listing Files

The files under a folder, whether a location or the whole project directory, are every file at any depth, hidden ones included, leaving out `.git` and whatever the project's `.gitignore` files ignore. They are shown by their path relative to the project, and sorted by it.
The spec files are the .pi files under the spec location, and the source files are the files under the code location. A use can leave out more, or cap how many it takes.

    /// The counts that aren't zero, in words.
    pub fn changes(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        [
            (self.modified, "modified"),
            (self.added, "added"),
            (self.deleted, "deleted"),
            (self.renamed, "renamed"),

        ]

# GPUI Kit Assets

> [!NOTE]
> **The complete catalog does not make existing applications embed every icon.**
> `Assets` keeps the original 101 component icons. Applications provide additional
> icons through their own `AssetSource`, as before; they do not need to redeclare
> the component icons. Only explicitly registering `AllAssets` embeds all 1,830
> SVGs on native platforms. Depending on the crate or using the shared `IconName`
> alone does not reference every SVG payload.
>
> | Native asset configuration | Embedded SVG data | Binary increase vs. default `Assets` |
> | --- | ---: | ---: |
> | Default component icons (101) | 44.28 KiB | 0 B (baseline) |
> | Default + 2 application icons (103) | 45.04 KiB | +15.19 KiB |
> | Default + 10 application icons (111) | 48.09 KiB | +19.19 KiB |
> | Explicit `AllAssets` (1,830) | 731.45 KiB | +1.02 MiB |
>
> **In this example, adding 10 application icons costs about 19 KiB, not the full
> catalog.** Their SVGs total 3,903 bytes; the measured binary increase is 19,648
> bytes, including the extra source's lookup/list-composition code, metadata and
> alignment. These are not fixed per-icon costs or whole-application sizes.
>
> Measured with Lucide 1.43.0 on Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0, `--release`, and stripped
> symbols. Each program uses the same `IconName` lookup and runtime asset path.
> The extra source falls back to `Assets`, and merges, sorts and deduplicates both
> sources' lists. The 10 extras are `Accessibility`, `AlarmClock`, `Archive`,
> `Award`, `Backpack`, `Bike`, `Bird`, `Camera`, `Coffee` and `Compass`; the two-icon
> case uses the first two. SVG complexity, toolchain and source implementation
> change the result.

input.message:
The left sidebar now follows the mockup's layout and the spec: the tree, the git panel's header and body, and no line between the panels. `cargo build` has no warnings. The full suite ran 358 passed, 2 failed, 1 ignored, and both failures are the known unrelated ones. Nothing was committed, and spec/, .claude/ and CLAUDE.md are untouched.

## What changed
Paths are under /home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl/src/.

**Theme** (`theme.rs`)
- New `darkest` colour (:40): #111111 in dark mode (:81) and #e1e1e1 in light mode (:114). Light mode is one step lighter than the ribbon's command area, the same 0x11 step the ribbon uses.

**Ribbon** (`ribbon/mod.rs`)
- `command_shades` (:917) and `command_colors` (:937) are now `pub(crate)` so Commit can use the ribbon's button colour. The only change is the visibility keyword.

**Tree** (`project_tree.rs`)
- Row constants at :38–60: 24px rows, 24px indent per level, the selection inset 8px, the first icon 16px from the tree's edge, the name 8px after its icon, rounded corners, and hover at half strength.
- `Locations` (:159) reads `root` and `codeRoot` from piton.config.pi. It is re-read when a project opens and whenever the project's root folder is re-read.
- `IconTint`, `Look` and `look()` (:182–250) decide each row's icon, icon colour and dimming:
  - Folders use a folder icon, the same open or closed; `.pi` files a code-file icon; `piton.config.pi` a settings-file icon in orange; other files a text-file icon.
  - The spec folder and the `.pi` files under it take Spec's colour; the code folder takes Code's colour (`chat_input::mode_color`).
  - Dot files and folders are dimmed, except .gitignore-like files. Anything git ignores is dimmed too.
- `render_entry` (:899) no longer uses `ListItem` and has no chevrons. The selected row gets the ribbon colour (#222222), rounded, with a semibold name; hover is fainter. Dimming wins over git-status colour on the name, as the mockup shows for .suspense. Inline naming, the diff button and the context menu still work.
- The tree sits on `darkest` (:1254).

**Git panel** (`git_panel.rs`)
- The header (:784) is 32px on #333333, with the branch in regular text and square ghost pull/push buttons.
- The body (:867) is on #222222 with 8px side and bottom padding and 4px gaps. The summary line is small and muted, with +/− in green and red on the right.
- Notes are now wrapping, auto-growing text areas (:471) in square #333333 boxes. The remove button only appears while the note is hovered.
- The message box is on #111111, reads "Commit Message…" (:409), and is monospace as before.
- "Generate" (sparkles, #333333) is at the left (:834) and "Commit" (#444444) at the right (:855), both square and 22px tall; Commit lost its icon.
- A `flush()` helper (:718) strips the fixed padding gpui-kit puts inside multi-line inputs, which can't be configured, so notes and the message match the mockup's sizes. The message's grow-to-fit tracker now sits inside that wrapper; outside it, the tracker measured the padding and collapsed the box.
- `COLOUR_IS_EDGE` (:35) records that the header's colour is its top edge.

**Sidebar and main window**
- `sidebar.rs` has a new `between()` (:45) that leaves out the line when the next panel's colour change is its edge.
- `main_window.rs` uses it (:1662), so there is no line between the tree and the git panel. I also removed the `FluentBuilder` import, which that change left unused.

**Test helper** (`frame_image.rs`)
- New `Frame` (:87) reads the colour at a point in a rendered frame.

## Where it differs from the mockup
- **Spec and code folder colours:** they use the theme's mode colours (#7fb4ea blue, #f0928a red), as the spec says, not the mockup's darker #6386d1 and #ca666f. Their darkness points to screenshot sampling rather than different colours.
- **Dimmed text:** it uses tertiary text (#9c9c9c), as the spec says. The mockup's brightest dimmed pixel is about #777777.
- **Icon colour:** most icons are muted (#c4c4c4), as the spec says. The mockup's folder and file icons are the full text colour (#dddddd).
- **Scrollbar:** the spec requires a permanent 18px scroll column that the mockup doesn't show. The selection is therefore inset 8px from the scrolling area, not from the panel's edge.
- **Plain file icon:** I used a text-file icon (lines) to match the mockup. The spec only says "an outlined file icon".
- **Enter in notes:** since notes are now multi-line text areas, Enter adds a line break inside a note.

## Tests
New tests:
- **Row height and indent:** `project_tree::rows_are_24px_tall_and_indented_24px_a_level`
- **Selected-row background:** `project_tree::the_selected_row_is_on_the_ribbons_colour` (dark and light)
- **Icon colours and dimming:** `project_tree::locations_colour_their_icons_and_dot_files_are_dimmed` and `location_colours_are_the_modes`
- **No line between the panels:**
  - `main_window::no_line_lies_between_the_tree_and_the_git_panel` (a git repo shaped like the mockup, dark and light, with the double-border check)
  - `sidebar::a_line_lies_between_panels_unless_colour_is_the_edge`
- **Git header and body colours:** `git_panel::the_header_and_body_take_the_ribbons_colours` (32px header, colours, padding and gaps, wrapping notes, darkest message box, nothing rounded; dark and light)
- **Generate/Commit placement:** `git_panel::generate_is_at_the_left_and_commit_at_the_right`
- **Theme:** `theme::the_darkest_surface_steps_past_the_ribbon`

The existing tree, git panel and sidebar tests pass unchanged, apart from making the note boxes, summary and tree area findable by tests. The 29 sidebar-related tests passed on three repeated runs.

**Full suite:** 358 passed, 2 failed, 1 ignored.

**Known unrelated failures (not caused by this work):**
- `system_prompts::tests::defaults_are_this_repositorys_templates`
- `prompt_mode::tests::selected_answer_text_can_be_copied_or_attached`

The intermittent prompt_mode/harness tests didn't fail this time.

I rustfmt'd project_tree.rs, git_panel.rs and frame_image.rs, which were clean at HEAD, and fixed formatting by hand in my own main_window.rs test. rustfmt still reports differences in main_window.rs and ribbon/mod.rs, but only in code I didn't touch, so I left them.

The left sidebar now matches your mockup's layout and sizes. The 25 sidebar tests pass when I run them; nothing is committed.

**File tree:**
- **Rows:** 24px rows on a #111111 background, with no chevrons; clicking a folder opens or closes it. Each level is indented 24px.
- **Selected row:** #222222 with softly rounded corners and a semibold name. Hovered rows get a fainter version of the same.
- **Icons:** outline folder and file icons. `.pi` files get a code-file icon, and `piton.config.pi` gets an orange settings icon.
- **Coloured folders:** the spec folder is blue, as are the `.pi` files in it, and the code folder is red. Only the icons are coloured, and the folders are read from `piton.config.pi`.
- **Dimmed entries:** anything starting with a dot is dimmed (except `.gitignore`-style files), and so is anything git ignores.
- **Unchanged:** git-status colouring, the diff button, the right-click menu and inline renaming still work.

**Git panel:**
- **Header:** the branch row is now a 32px header on #333333, with a branch icon, the name, and cloud-download/cloud-upload icons for pull and push. There's no line between it and the tree.
- **Body:** #222222 with 8px padding. The change summary is small and muted, with +/− at the right.
- **Commit notes:** square #333333 boxes whose text wraps. The remove button only appears while you hover a note.
- **Message box:** #111111, monospace, reading "Commit Message…".
- **Buttons:** "Generate" (was "Write message") is at the bottom left and "Commit" at the right.

The spec changes are in `spec/ui/components/file-tree/index.pi` (a new "look" section), `spec/ui/components/git-panel/index.pi`, and the rule for lines between sidebar panels. Check, format check and build all pass.

**Where it differs from the mockup:**
- **Folder colours:** the spec and code folders use the app's Spec blue and Code red, which are a bit brighter than the mockup's.
- **Dimmed entries and icons:** dimmed entries are a lighter grey (#9c9c9c) than the mockup's, and most icons are slightly muted rather than full white.
- **Scrollbar:** the tree keeps a permanent 18px scrollbar column that your mockup doesn't show. So the selected row's highlight is inset from the scroll area, not the panel edge.
- **Enter in notes:** commit notes are now multi-line boxes, so Enter adds a line break inside a note.

If you want the icons at full white, the scrollbar hidden until needed, or the mockup's exact colours, say so and I'll update the spec.

**Tests:** the full suite has 358 passing and 2 failing. The failures are the known ones: `defaults_are_this_repositorys_templates` and `selected_answer_text_can_be_copied_or_attached`.

There's now a very large amount of uncommitted work (everything since the usage popover), so it's worth committing soon.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors still need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings. The `backlog` MCP server still can't connect because its executable isn't on your PATH.
